## What "writing a function" means

A worker contributes capabilities to an iii system by registering functions. Each function has an
`id` of the form `service::name`, a handler that receives the payload and returns a result, and
optional JSON Schemas that describe the request and response shape.

The `function_id` is the contract. Callers invoke the function, and observers run a target on each
call; see [Using iii / Functions](../using-iii/functions).

## Register a function

Inside the worker, register the function with the SDK. The `id` is what callers and observers use as
a `function_id`.

<Note>
  A function that is an observer's target receives what the observed function's documentation
  describes. For example, a target of `cron::on-tick` with `deliver: "input"` receives the tick, and
  a target of `http::on-request` receives an HTTP request with `body`, `headers`, and other
  properties. Each worker's page at [workers.iii.dev](https://workers.iii.dev/) lists its functions,
  their input, and their `args`.
</Note>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    worker.registerFunction("math::add", async (payload: { a: number; b: number }) => {
      return { c: payload.a + payload.b };
    });
    ```

## Attach request and response schemas

Attach JSON Schemas to the registration so the request and response shape are documented alongside
the function. The schemas are stored with the function and surface in the iii console,
`iii call <function_id> --help`, and elsewhere.

<Note>
  Runtime validation is not yet supported. Attached schemas are metadata only; the engine does not
  enforce a specific schema, reject payloads, nor handler return values that don't match the
  schemas. Treat the schemas as contract documentation for function invocations, agents, and the
  console.
</Note>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    worker.registerFunction(
      "math::add",
      async (payload: { a: number; b: number }) => ({ c: payload.a + payload.b }),
      {
        request_format: {
          type: "object",
          properties: { a: { type: "number" }, b: { type: "number" } },
          required: ["a", "b"],
        },
        response_format: {
          type: "object",
          properties: { c: { type: "number" } },
          required: ["c"],
        },
      },
    );
    ```

  </Tab>

    def add_handler(payload: dict) -> dict:
        return {"c": payload["a"] + payload["b"]}

    worker.register_function(
        "math::add",
        add_handler,
        request_format={
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"a": {"type": "number"}, "b": {"type": "number"}},
            "required": ["a", "b"],

        response_format={
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"c": {"type": "number"}},

    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::{register_worker, InitOptions, RegisterFunction};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct AddInput {
        a: f64,
        b: f64,
    }

    #[derive(Serialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct AddOutput {
        c: f64,
    }

    fn main() {
        let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
        let worker = register_worker(
            &url,
            InitOptions {
                namespace: Some("orders".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        );

        // The closure's input and output types give the schemas: schemars derives
        // `request_format` from `AddInput` and `response_format` from `AddOutput`.
        // No builder methods are needed.
        worker.register_function(
            "math::add",
            RegisterFunction::new(|input: AddInput| -> Result<AddOutput, iii_sdk::Error> {
                Ok(AddOutput { c: input.a + input.b })
            }),
        );
    }
    ```

    type AddInput struct {
    	A float64 `json:"a" jsonschema:"required"`
    	B float64 `json:"b" jsonschema:"required"`
    }

    type AddOutput struct {
    	C float64 `json:"c" jsonschema:"required"`
    }

    func main() {
    	client := iii.RegisterWorker(os.Getenv("III_URL"), iii.WithNamespace("orders"))

    	// The schemas are reflected from AddInput and AddOutput at registration;
    	// shape them with `json` and `jsonschema` struct tags.
    	if _, err := iii.RegisterFunctionTyped(client, "math::add", func(ctx context.Context, input AddInput) (AddOutput, error) {
    		return AddOutput{C: input.A + input.B}, nil
    	}); err != nil {
    		log.Fatal(err)
    	}
    }

## Attach metadata

`metadata` is an arbitrary JSON object stored with the function at registration. The engine never
interprets it, it's stored with the function so other parts of the system can act on it. It surfaces
in `engine::functions::info`, the iii console, and is commonly used with `iii-worker-manager` / Role
based access control.

Because the shape is entirely yours, metadata is a facility that can enable and enhance other
functionality. For example,
[worker-manager RBAC allowlists](./worker-manager#trusted-and-rbac-listeners) can expose functions
by a `metadata:` selector, so tagging a function `{ public: true }` or `{ tier: "premium" }` lets
you gate access on the fields you define.

<Warning>
  All access should be gated system-side. You should never rely on an untrusted worker to define
  what they can or can't have access to.
</Warning>

    worker.registerFunction(
      "math::add",

## Receive per-invocation metadata

Each function can also receive optional per-invocation `metadata`: any JSON value. A caller sets it
on the call, and an observer sets it once for every activation of its target, to give the receiving
function execution context (see [Policy and metadata](../using-iii/observers#policy-and-metadata)).
A call through an observer takes no metadata of its own: its target receives the observer's.

`null` is the same as no metadata. A call that carries no metadata reaches the handler with none,
whether it runs in the same worker or goes through the engine.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    // The second argument is `undefined` when the call carries no metadata.
    worker.registerFunction(
      "math::add",
      async (payload: { a: number; b: number }, metadata) => ({
        c: payload.a + payload.b,
        metadata,
      }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import os

    from iii import InitOptions, register_worker

    worker = register_worker(
        os.environ["III_URL"],
        InitOptions(worker_name="math-worker", namespace="orders"),
    )

    # Metadata reaches a handler only when it declares a parameter named `metadata`
    # (positional or keyword-only); other signatures are called as before. The
    # parameter is `None` when the call carries no metadata.
    def add_handler(payload: dict, metadata=None) -> dict:
        return {"c": payload["a"] + payload["b"], "metadata": metadata}

    worker.register_function("math::add", add_handler)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::{register_worker, InitOptions, RegisterFunction};
    use serde_json::{json, Value};

    fn main() {
        let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
        let worker = register_worker(
            &url,
            InitOptions {
                namespace: Some("orders".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        );

        // A two-argument closure receives the metadata as `Option<Value>`;
        // one-argument closures keep working unchanged.
        worker.register_function(
            "math::add",
            RegisterFunction::new_async(|input: Value, metadata: Option<Value>| async move {
                let a = input["a"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
                let b = input["b"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
                Ok(json!({ "c": a + b, "metadata": metadata }))
            }),
        );
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
    	"context"
    	"encoding/json"
    	"log"
    	"os"

    	iii "github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii"
    )

    func main() {
    	client := iii.RegisterWorker(os.Getenv("III_URL"), iii.WithNamespace("orders"))

    	// MetadataFromContext reports false when the call carries none.
    	_, err := client.RegisterFunction("math::add", func(ctx context.Context, data json.RawMessage) (any, error) {
    		var payload struct {
    			A float64 `json:"a"`
    			B float64 `json:"b"`
    		}
    		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &payload); err != nil {
    			return nil, err
    		}
    		metadata, _ := iii.MetadataFromContext(ctx)
    		return map[string]any{"c": payload.A + payload.B, "metadata": metadata}, nil
    	})
    	if err != nil {
    		log.Fatal(err)
    	}
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Note>
  Registration metadata is a different field from per-invocation metadata. It is set once on the
  registration and the engine stores it with the function; the per-invocation value travels on each
  call and reaches the handler.
</Note>

## HTTP-invoked functions

A worker can register a function that the engine invokes over HTTP. The registration carries an
`HttpInvocationConfig` instead of a handler: the engine makes the HTTP call whenever the function is
invoked, and the worker declares only the endpoint.

This is the mechanism that surfaces an existing API gateway, webhook, serverless platform (Lambda,
Azure Functions, Google Cloud Functions), or third-party API as a regular iii function.

`iii-http-functions` is one worker that uses this mechanism; its
[Worker Docs](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/iii-http-functions) describe its configuration and
security controls.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    worker.registerFunction(
      "math::multiply",
      {
        url: "https://math.example.com/multiply",
        method: "POST",
        timeout_ms: 5000,
        headers: { "X-Service": "iii-worker" },
        auth: { type: "bearer", token_key: "MATH_API_TOKEN" },
      },
      { description: "Multiply two numbers in the math service" },
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import os

    from iii import InitOptions, register_worker
    from iii_helpers.http import HttpAuthBearer, HttpInvocationConfig

    worker = register_worker(
        os.environ["III_URL"],
        InitOptions(worker_name="math-worker", namespace="orders"),
    )

    worker.register_function(
        "math::multiply",
        HttpInvocationConfig(
            url="https://math.example.com/multiply",
            method="POST",
            timeout_ms=5000,
            headers={"X-Service": "iii-worker"},
            auth=HttpAuthBearer(token_key="MATH_API_TOKEN"),
        ),
        description="Multiply two numbers in the math service",
    )
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_helpers::http::{HttpAuthConfig, HttpInvocationConfig, HttpMethod};
    use iii_sdk::{register_worker, InitOptions, RegisterFunction};
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    fn main() {
        let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
        let worker = register_worker(
            &url,
            InitOptions {
                namespace: Some("orders".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        );

        let mut headers = HashMap::new();
        headers.insert("X-Service".to_string(), "iii-worker".to_string());

        let config = HttpInvocationConfig {
            url: "https://math.example.com/multiply".to_string(),
            method: HttpMethod::Post,
            timeout_ms: Some(5000),
            headers,
            auth: Some(HttpAuthConfig::Bearer {
                token_key: "MATH_API_TOKEN".to_string(),
            }),
        };

        worker.register_function(
            "math::multiply",
            RegisterFunction::http(config).description("Multiply two numbers in the math service"),
        );
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
    	"log"
    	"os"

    	iii "github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii"
    )

    func main() {
    	client := iii.RegisterWorker(os.Getenv("III_URL"), iii.WithNamespace("orders"))

    	timeoutMs := uint64(5000)
    	_, err := client.RegisterHTTPFunction(
    		"math::multiply",
    		iii.HTTPInvocationRef{
    			URL:       "https://math.example.com/multiply",
    			Method:    "POST",
    			TimeoutMs: &timeoutMs,
    			Headers:   map[string]string{"X-Service": "iii-worker"},
    			Auth:      iii.BearerAuth("MATH_API_TOKEN"),
    		},
    		iii.RegisterFunctionOptions{Description: "Multiply two numbers in the math service"},
    	)
    	if err != nil {
    		log.Fatal(err)
    	}
    }
    ```

### `HttpInvocationConfig` fields

A handler function takes an `id` and a handler. An HTTP-invoked function takes an `id` and an
`HttpInvocationConfig`, and no handler runs in the worker.

| Field        | Type                                              | Default    | Description                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `url`        | `string`                                          | (required) | Endpoint the engine calls when the function is invoked.                                                      |
| `method`     | `"GET" \| "POST" \| "PUT" \| "PATCH" \| "DELETE"` | `"POST"`   | HTTP method.                                                                                                 |
| `timeout_ms` | `number`                                          | `30000`    | Per-request timeout in milliseconds.                                                                         |
| `headers`    | `Record<string, string>`                          | `{}`       | Headers added to every invocation.                                                                           |
| `auth`       | `HttpAuthConfig`                                  | (none)     | `{ type: "bearer", token_key }`, `{ type: "hmac", secret_key }`, or `{ type: "api_key", header, value_key }` |

<Note>
  Auth fields (`token_key`, `secret_key`, `value_key`) are specified as the **names of environment
  variables**, not the secrets themselves. The engine resolves them from its own process environment
  at registration time, so secrets stay on the engine host and never travel over the SDK WebSocket.
</Note>

### HTTP error handling

The engine sends the invocation payload as the JSON request body. It treats every response with a
status below 400 as a success, and every other response, or a network error, as an invocation
failure that propagates back to the caller. A 1xx or 3xx response is a success with no function
result.

HTTP-invoked functions appear in
[`engine::functions::list`](../using-iii/functions#engine-functions-engine) and are discoverable
through the console exactly like in-process handlers.

## Return values and errors

A handler returns a value that matches its documented
[response schema](#attach-request-and-response-schemas), or an error. An error raised in the handler
reaches the caller as an invocation error, with the handler's `error.stack` attached in Node. The
engine does not swallow it.

Return a structured value for an expected failure, and throw for an unexpected one.

## Observers of a function

Every registered function is observable unless the registration sets `observable: false`, which
makes the engine refuse every observer with `NOT_OBSERVABLE`; the function stays callable.
`private: true` allows calls only from the connection that hosts the function, and other workers can
still observe it. `args_format` is the JSON Schema of the args an observer passes.

See [Observable functions](./observable-functions) for the hooks that run around observation.

## Unregister a function

`registerFunction` returns a handle with an `unregister()` method that removes the function from the
engine at runtime. When the worker disconnects, all of its functions are removed automatically and
pending invocations error out.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    const add = worker.registerFunction("math::add", async (payload: { a: number; b: number }) => {
      return { c: payload.a + payload.b };
    });

    add.unregister();
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import os

    from iii import InitOptions, register_worker

    worker = register_worker(
        os.environ["III_URL"],
        InitOptions(worker_name="math-worker", namespace="orders"),
    )

    def add_handler(payload: dict) -> dict:
        return {"c": payload["a"] + payload["b"]}

    add = worker.register_function("math::add", add_handler)

    add.unregister()
    ```

  </Tab>

    use iii_sdk::{register_worker, InitOptions, RegisterFunction};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct AddInput {
        a: f64,
        b: f64,
    }

    fn main() {
        let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
        let worker = register_worker(
            &url,
            InitOptions {
                namespace: Some("orders".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        );

        let add = worker.register_function(
            "math::add",
            RegisterFunction::new(|input: AddInput| {
                Ok(serde_json::json!({ "c": input.a + input.b }))
            }),
        );

        add.unregister();
    }

    package main

    import (

    func main() {

    		var payload struct {

    		}
    		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &payload); err != nil {
